database: local synthetic copy of JMS staging (seed 7, cap 3000)

cases.question: Show me all active surrogates in Screening and list their current substage.
cases.title: Active surrogates in Screening with current substage
cases.sql:
SELECT g.case_id AS case_id, g.case_file_name AS surrogate_case, t.title AS current_substage
FROM gc_case g
LEFT JOIN custom_sub_stage s ON s.sub_stage_id = (
    SELECT s2.sub_stage_id FROM custom_sub_stage s2
    WHERE s2.gc_case_id = g.case_id AND s2.stage = 'screening' AND s2.completed IS NULL
    ORDER BY s2.ordering, s2.sub_stage_id LIMIT 1)
LEFT JOIN template_sub_stage t ON t.sub_stage_id = s.base_sub_stage_id
WHERE g.case_type = 'surrogate' AND g.active = 1 AND g.stage = 'screening'
ORDER BY g.case_file_name
assumptions: Surrogates are cases of type surrogate; active means the case is flagged active (not archived/inactive).
In Screening means the case's current stage is screening.
Current substage is the first not-yet-completed screening substage in workflow order for that case.
Surrogates in Screening with no screening substage assigned are still listed, with the substage left blank.
The case file name is used as the surrogate's name.

cases.question: Which IP cases are in matching right now? Include the names and emails for both IPs.
cases.title: IP cases currently in matching, with both intended parents' names and emails
cases.sql: SELECT ic.case_id AS case_number, ic.case_file_name AS case_name, CONCAT_WS(' ', c1.first_name, c1.last_name) AS ip_1_name, c1.email AS ip_1_email, CONCAT_WS(' ', c2.first_name, c2.last_name) AS ip_2_name, c2.email AS ip_2_email FROM ip_case ic JOIN family f ON f.family_id = ic.family_id JOIN contact c1 ON c1.contact_id = f.ip_1_id LEFT JOIN contact c2 ON c2.contact_id = f.ip_2_id WHERE ic.stage = 'matching' AND ic.active = 1 ORDER BY ic.case_id
assumptions: 'In matching right now' means the case's current workflow stage is Matching.
Only active cases are included; one inactive case in the matching stage is left out.
'Both IPs' means the first and second intended parents on the family record. Many families have only one, so the second name and email are blank for those cases.

cases.question: Which cases have had their profiles approved in the last 30 days?
cases.title: Cases with profile approved in the last 30 days
cases.sql:
select 'Intended parent' as `Case type`, ic.case_id as `Case ID`, ic.case_file_name as `Case name`, ic.stage as `Stage`, f.profile_approved as `Profile approved on` from ip_case ic join family f on f.family_id=ic.family_id where f.profile_approved >= date_sub(now(), interval 30 day) and f.profile_approved<=now()
union all
select case gc.case_type when 'surrogate' then 'Surrogate' when 'donor' then 'Egg donor' else 'Sperm donor' end, gc.case_id, gc.case_file_name, gc.stage, case gc.case_type when 'surrogate' then c.gc_profile_approved when 'donor' then c.ed_profile_approved else c.sd_profile_approved end from gc_case gc join contact c on c.contact_id=gc.gc_id where (case gc.case_type when 'surrogate' then c.gc_profile_approved when 'donor' then c.ed_profile_approved else c.sd_profile_approved end) >= date_sub(now(), interval 30 day) and (case gc.case_type when 'surrogate' then c.gc_profile_approved when 'donor' then c.ed_profile_approved else c.sd_profile_approved end) <= now()
order by `Profile approved on` desc
assumptions: 'Last 30 days' means the 30 days up to today (2026-10-21).
For intended-parent cases, profile approval is the approval date on the family record linked to the case.
For surrogate, egg donor and sperm donor cases, profile approval is the matching approval date on the person's contact record (surrogate, egg donor or sperm donor profile).
All case types are included. Currently only intended-parent cases have approvals in this window: 2 cases.

A specific intended parent (IP) case – please give the case ID or the parents' name

cases.question: List all overdue tasks across my journeys.
cases.title: Overdue tasks across journeys
cases.sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(ip.case_file_name, gc.case_file_name) AS journey,
  CASE WHEN t.ip_case_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'Intended parent' ELSE CONCAT('Journey - ', gc.case_type) END AS journey_type,
  t.task_title AS task,
  t.task_type AS task_type,
  t.task_status AS task_status,
  t.must_be_completed_by AS due_date,
  t.must_be_completed_time AS due_time,
  DATEDIFF('2026-10-21', t.must_be_completed_by) AS days_overdue,
  CONCAT(a.first_name, ' ', a.last_name) AS task_assigned_to
FROM case_task t
LEFT JOIN ip_case ip ON ip.case_id = t.ip_case_id
LEFT JOIN gc_case gc ON gc.case_id = t.gc_case_id
LEFT JOIN admin a ON a.admin_id = t.task_assigned_to_id
WHERE (t.ip_case_id IS NOT NULL OR t.gc_case_id IS NOT NULL)
  AND t.completed IS NULL
  AND t.task_status <> 'completed'
  AND t.must_be_completed_by < '2026-10-21'
ORDER BY t.must_be_completed_by, t.must_be_completed_time
assumptions: I couldn't tell which staff member you are, so this lists overdue tasks for all journeys, not only yours. The assigned person is shown so you can filter to yourself.
A journey means an intended-parent case or a donor/surrogate case.
A task is overdue if its due date is before today (2026-10-21) and it isn't complete.
A task counts as complete if it has a completion timestamp or its status is 'completed'. Deferred and pending tasks still count as overdue.
Tasks not linked to any journey are left out.

cases.question: List egg donors available for a cycle who haven't donated before.
cases.title: Available egg donors who have not donated before
cases.sql:
SELECT g.case_id AS case_number, g.case_file_name AS donor_case_name, c.contact_id AS donor_contact_id, c.first_name AS first_name, c.last_name AS last_name, c.email AS email, g.donor_status AS donor_availability, g.stage AS case_stage, p.past_donor AS donated_before_flag
FROM gc_case g
JOIN contact c ON c.contact_id = g.gc_id
JOIN ed_profile p ON p.contact_id = c.contact_id
WHERE g.case_type = 'donor'
  AND g.active = 1
  AND g.donor_status = 'available'
  AND p.past_donor = 0
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ed_profile p2 WHERE p2.contact_id = c.contact_id AND p2.past_donor = 1)
assumptions: Egg donors are donor-type cases; 'available for a cycle' means the donor's availability status is 'available' (not in a cycle, under review or temporarily unavailable).
Only active cases are included.

'Haven't donated before' means the donor's profile explicitly says they are not a past donor. Donors with no answer recorded or no profile are excluded, and so is any donor with another profile marked as a past donor.
Most available donors have no past-donor answer on file (9 of 10 available donors), so this list is short. Including those would make it much longer.

cases.question: Which contracts are still waiting on a signature?
cases.title: Contracts still waiting on a signature
cases.sql:
SELECT h.hellosign_id AS `Signature Request #`,
       h.created AS `Request Created`,
       CONCAT(a.first_name, ' ', a.last_name) AS `Requested By`,
       cr.user_type AS `Signer Type`,
       CASE cr.user_type
            WHEN 'user' THEN CONCAT(u.first_name, ' ', u.last_name)
            WHEN 'np_user' THEN CONCAT(np.first_name, ' ', np.last_name)
            WHEN 'admin' THEN CONCAT(sa.first_name, ' ', sa.last_name)
       END AS `Signer`,
       cr.status AS `Signature Status`,
       cr.created AS `Sent To Signer On`,
       DATEDIFF(CURDATE(), cr.created) AS `Days Waiting`
FROM contract_rel cr
JOIN hellosign h ON h.hellosign_id = cr.parent_id
LEFT JOIN admin a ON a.admin_id = h.created_by_id
LEFT JOIN user u ON cr.user_type = 'user' AND u.user_id = cr.user_id
LEFT JOIN user_np np ON cr.user_type = 'np_user' AND np.np_user_id = cr.user_id
LEFT JOIN admin sa ON cr.user_type = 'admin' AND sa.admin_id = cr.user_id
WHERE cr.status <> 'signed'
ORDER BY cr.created
assumptions: A contract is 'waiting on a signature' when a signer on its signature request has not yet signed; that includes requests that were sent, viewed, or could not be delivered.
Each row is one signer on one signature request, so a request with several unsigned signers appears more than once.
Signer names come from the matching user, partner/spouse or admin record depending on the signer type.
Days waiting is counted from when the request was sent to that signer until today.

cases.question: Show me which intended parents have never logged into their portal.
cases.title: Intended parents who have never logged into their portal
cases.sql: SELECT u.user_id AS `User ID`, u.first_name AS `First Name`, u.last_name AS `Last Name`, u.email AS `Email`, u.created AS `Account Created`, CASE WHEN u.active = 1 THEN 'Active' ELSE 'Inactive' END AS `Account Status`, CASE WHEN u.confirmed_email = 1 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS `Email Confirmed` FROM `user` u WHERE u.user_type = 'IP' AND u.last_login IS NULL ORDER BY u.created DESC
assumptions: Intended parents are user accounts of type 'IP'. IP representatives are not included.
Someone has 'never logged in' if their account has no recorded last-login time.
Active and inactive accounts are both included, and the report shows each account's status.
The report lists individual parent accounts, not cases or families. Accounts can't be reliably tied to a case or family in this data.

cases.question: How many open To Dos does each admin currently have assigned to them?
cases.title: Open To Dos currently assigned to each admin
cases.sql:
SELECT a.first_name AS first_name, a.last_name AS last_name,
  SUM(t.src = 'case') AS open_case_todos,
  SUM(t.src = 'general') AS open_general_todos,
  SUM(t.src = 'contact') AS open_contact_todos,
  COUNT(*) AS total_open_todos
FROM (
  SELECT 'case' AS src, task_assigned_to_id FROM case_task WHERE completed IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'general', task_assigned_to_id FROM general_task WHERE completed IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'contact', task_assigned_to_id FROM contact_task WHERE completed IS NULL
) t
JOIN admin a ON a.admin_id = t.task_assigned_to_id
GROUP BY a.admin_id, a.first_name, a.last_name
ORDER BY total_open_todos DESC, a.last_name, a.first_name
assumptions: 'To Dos' covers all three kinds of tasks: case tasks, general tasks and contact tasks. They are shown in separate columns plus a total.
A To Do is open if it has no completion date, whatever its status label says (the status label is rarely set to completed even for finished tasks). Deferred and pending tasks count as open.
Only admins with at least one open To Do are listed.
Tasks with no assigned admin are excluded.
Overdue and future-dated open To Dos are both counted.

cases.question: Which surrogates are still waiting on their profile to be approved?
cases.title: Surrogates still waiting on profile approval
cases.sql:
SELECT ct.contact_id AS "Contact ID", ct.first_name AS "First name", ct.last_name AS "Last name", ct.email AS "Email", g.case_file_name AS "Case name", g.stage AS "Case stage", s.status AS "Case status", a.first_name AS "Assigned admin first name", g.created AS "Case created"
FROM gc_case g
JOIN contact ct ON ct.contact_id = g.gc_id
LEFT JOIN status s ON s.status_id = g.status_id
LEFT JOIN admin a ON a.admin_id = g.assigned_admin
WHERE g.case_type = 'surrogate'
  AND g.active = 1
  AND ct.gc_profile_approved IS NULL
ORDER BY g.created
assumptions: Surrogates are cases of type 'surrogate' (not egg or sperm donors).
'Waiting on profile approval' means the surrogate's profile has no approval date recorded yet.
Only active cases are included; archived or inactive cases are left out.
A surrogate with more than one active case appears once per case.

cases.question: Show me egg donor profiles that haven't been approved by the agency yet.
cases.title: Egg donor profiles not yet approved by the agency
cases.sql:
SELECT c.contact_id AS contact_id, c.first_name AS first_name, c.last_name AS last_name, c.email AS email, c.created AS contact_created, s.status AS current_status, COUNT(e.profile_id) AS profile_records, MAX(e.profile_id) AS latest_profile_id
FROM contact c
JOIN ed_profile e ON e.contact_id = c.contact_id
LEFT JOIN status s ON s.status_id = c.status_id
WHERE c.ed_profile_approved IS NULL
GROUP BY c.contact_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, c.email, c.created, s.status
ORDER BY c.created DESC
assumptions: An egg donor profile is a contact that has an egg donor profile record on file.
A profile counts as not yet approved by the agency when the contact has no egg donor profile approval date.
Some donors have more than one profile record, so the report shows one row per donor and counts their profile records.
Newest contacts are listed first.

cases.question: Pull a list of sperm donors whose profiles are pending approval.
cases.title: Sperm donors with profiles pending approval
cases.sql:
SELECT c.contact_id AS `Contact ID`, c.first_name AS `First Name`, c.last_name AS `Last Name`, c.email AS `Email`, c.phone_number AS `Phone`, g.case_id AS `Case ID`, g.stage AS `Case Stage`, s.status AS `Case Status`, g.created AS `Case Created`
FROM gc_case g
JOIN contact c ON c.contact_id = g.gc_id
LEFT JOIN status s ON s.status_id = g.status_id
WHERE g.case_type = 'sperm_donor'
  AND g.active = 1
  AND c.sd_profile_approved IS NULL
ORDER BY g.created DESC
assumptions: Sperm donors are people who have a case of type sperm donor.
'Profile pending approval' means the donor's sperm donor profile has no approval date recorded yet.
Only active cases are included; archived or inactive cases are excluded.
This is based on the profile approval date, not the workflow status label 'Pending IP Approval'. Tell me if you meant that status instead.
A donor with more than one active sperm donor case appears once per case.

cases.question: Show me intended parents whose profile has been approved.
cases.title: Intended parents with an approved profile
cases.sql:
SELECT f.family_id AS family_id,
       ic.case_id AS case_id,
       ic.case_file_name AS case_name,
       CONCAT_WS(' ', c1.first_name, c1.last_name) AS intended_parent_1,
       CONCAT_WS(' ', c2.first_name, c2.last_name) AS intended_parent_2,
       f.profile_approved AS profile_approved_on,
       ic.stage AS case_stage,
       ic.active AS case_active
FROM family f
LEFT JOIN ip_case ic ON ic.family_id = f.family_id
LEFT JOIN contact c1 ON c1.contact_id = f.ip_1_id
LEFT JOIN contact c2 ON c2.contact_id = f.ip_2_id
WHERE f.profile_approved IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY f.profile_approved DESC
assumptions: An intended parent's profile counts as approved when the family record has a profile approval date.
Each row is a family and its intended-parent case; a family with several cases appears once per case, and one with no case appears with blank case details.
Both intended parents of the family are shown, with the second blank when there isn't one.
Newest approvals are listed first.
